front: Which git command shows the commit history in a compact, one-line-per-commit form?
back: git log --oneline
accepted_answers: git log --oneline
hint: Add --graph to visualize branch topology alongside it.

front: Which Maven lifecycle phase compiles, runs tests, and packages the project into a distributable artifact such as a jar?
back: package
accepted_answers: package
hint: Earlier phases like compile and test run automatically before it.

front: Which Docker command lists currently running containers?
back: docker ps
accepted_answers: docker ps
hint: Add -a to also show stopped containers.

front: What is the difference between git merge and git rebase when integrating a feature branch into main?
back: git merge creates a new merge commit that ties both histories together and preserves exactly what happened, while git rebase replays the feature branch's commits on top of main one by one, producing a linear history but rewriting the feature branch's commit hashes.
accepted_answers: merge preserves history with a merge commit; rebase replays commits onto main and rewrites their hashes for a linear history
hint: Never rebase commits that have already been pushed and shared with others.

front: Why does a multi-stage Dockerfile with a build stage plus a slim runtime stage produce smaller, more secure production images than a single-stage build?
back: The build stage can include heavy compilers, build tools, and source code needed only to produce the artifact, while the final runtime stage copies just the built artifact into a minimal base image, so build-time tooling and source never ship in the production image.
accepted_answers: the build stage's tooling and source are discarded; only the built artifact is copied into a minimal runtime image
hint: Each FROM in the Dockerfile can start a fresh stage that discards the previous stage's filesystem.

front: What is the difference between a rolling deployment and a blue-green deployment strategy?
back: A rolling deployment gradually replaces old instances with new ones a few at a time, keeping both versions briefly serving traffic together, while blue-green keeps two complete environments and switches all traffic from the old to the fully deployed new environment at once, enabling instant rollback by switching back.
accepted_answers: rolling replaces instances gradually; blue-green switches all traffic at once between two full environments
hint: Blue-green trades double the running infrastructure for an instant, low-risk rollback.

front: Why do semantic versioning rules of MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH matter for consumers of a published library?
back: Incrementing MAJOR signals a breaking change that may require consumer code updates, MINOR signals backward-compatible new functionality, and PATCH signals backward-compatible bug fixes, so consumers can safely automate upgrades within the same MAJOR version without expecting breakage.
accepted_answers: MAJOR signals breaking changes, MINOR adds compatible features, PATCH is compatible bug fixes
hint: A dependency range like caret 2.3.1 relies on this contract being honored.

front: What is the practical difference between a liveness probe and a readiness probe in a container orchestrator like Kubernetes?
back: A failing liveness probe tells the orchestrator the process is stuck or dead and should be restarted, while a failing readiness probe tells the orchestrator the instance is temporarily unable to serve traffic and should be removed from the load balancer without restarting it.
accepted_answers: liveness failure triggers a restart; readiness failure only removes the instance from traffic without restarting it
hint: A slow database dependency should usually fail readiness, not liveness.

front: Running git status right after git add on a modified file, before any commit, shows the file under which section?
back: Changes to be committed
accepted_answers: Changes to be committed
hint: Staged changes are listed separately from unstaged working-tree changes.

front: A Dockerfile copies pom.xml and downloads dependencies before copying the rest of the source and building. A rebuild happens after only an application source file changed, with pom.xml untouched. Which layers does Docker reuse from cache and which does it rebuild?
back: The dependency-download layer is reused from cache since pom.xml did not change, but the layer that copies the rest of the source and every layer after it are rebuilt because the source file changed, which is exactly why dependencies are copied and downloaded before the rest of the source.
accepted_answers: the cached dependency layer is reused; the source-copy layer and everything after it rebuilds
hint: Docker invalidates a layer's cache, and every layer after it, once its inputs change.

front: A CI pipeline runs mvn test and one test fails. What does the overall pipeline step typically report, assuming default Maven Surefire behavior?
back: The mvn command exits with a non-zero status because Surefire fails the build on a test failure by default, so the CI step is reported as failed and later pipeline stages are typically skipped.
accepted_answers: the build fails with a non-zero exit code because a failing test fails the Maven build by default
hint: A CI step's pass or fail state is driven by the invoked command's exit code.

front: After git rebase is used interactively to squash three commits into one on a local feature branch, what does a plain git push do when the remote branch already has the three original commits?
back: The push is rejected as a non-fast-forward update, because the rewritten local history no longer contains the original three commits as ancestors of the remote branch tip, so a force push, ideally force-with-lease, is required to overwrite the remote history.
accepted_answers: the push is rejected as non-fast-forward and requires a force push to overwrite remote history
hint: Rebase rewrites commit hashes, so the remote and local histories diverge even though the code content matches.

front: A production container repeatedly restarts in a crash loop immediately after deployment, and logs show it exiting with status 137. What is the most likely cause?
back: Exit code 137, which is 128 plus SIGKILL's signal number 9, typically means the container's process was killed by the out-of-memory killer because it exceeded its configured memory limit, so the fix is to raise the memory limit or reduce the application's memory usage.
accepted_answers: exit 137 indicates an out-of-memory kill; raise the memory limit or reduce memory usage
hint: 137 decodes as 128 plus the signal number 9, SIGKILL.

front: Two developers modify the same lines of the same file on separate branches, and merging the second branch into the first reports a merge conflict. What must happen before the merge can be completed?
back: Git cannot automatically decide which version, or combination, of the conflicting lines is correct, so a person must manually edit the conflict markers in the file to the intended final content and then stage and commit the resolved file to complete the merge.
accepted_answers: someone must manually resolve the conflicting lines and commit the resolved file
hint: Git marks the conflicting region with conflict markers directly in the file itself.

front: A CI build passes on a developer's machine but fails on the build server with "cannot find symbol" for a class that clearly exists in the source tree. What is a common cause in a Maven multi-module project?
back: The module containing that class was not built and installed before the failing module in the build order, due to a missing or misordered module dependency, or a stale local Maven cache on the developer's machine masking the real order problem, so the compiler cannot resolve a class from a module that has not been built yet.
accepted_answers: a missing or misordered module build dependency means the class's module has not been built yet
hint: Check the reactor build order and each module's declared dependencies in pom.xml.

front: A deployed application reads a database password from an environment variable, and after deployment it fails to start with an authentication error even though the intended password value is correct. What is a common environment-variable-related mistake that causes this?
back: The environment variable name is misspelled or not actually set in the deployment environment, for example a typo in a Kubernetes or Docker Compose config key, so the application receives an empty or missing value instead of the intended password, even though the correct password exists somewhere in configuration.
accepted_answers: the environment variable name is misspelled or not actually set or exported in that environment
hint: Confirm the variable is actually set at startup without logging its value.

front: A health check endpoint returns 200 immediately after the application process starts, but real requests fail for the next several seconds while a connection pool and cache warm up. What deployment problem does this cause, and what is the fix?
back: The orchestrator routes real traffic to the instance as soon as the health check passes, so requests fail during the warm-up window; the fix is to make the readiness check itself verify that dependencies like the pool and cache are actually initialized before reporting healthy, rather than just checking that the process is running.
accepted_answers: traffic is routed before warm-up finishes; fix by making the readiness check verify dependencies are actually initialized
hint: A readiness check should reflect can serve traffic now, not just process is alive.

front: Write a git command that creates and switches to a new branch named feature/login from the current branch.
back: git checkout -b feature/login
accepted_answers: git checkout -b feature/login
hint: -b creates the branch before switching to it.

front: Write a Dockerfile CMD instruction, in exec form, that runs a jar file named app.jar with java.
back: CMD ["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]
accepted_answers: CMD ["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]
hint: The exec form, a JSON array, avoids running the command through a shell.

front: Write a Maven command that builds the project while skipping test execution entirely.
back: mvn install -DskipTests
accepted_answers: mvn install -DskipTests
hint: -DskipTests still compiles tests; maven.test.skip=true skips compiling them too.
